Choose maximum modulus x1 and fix the other magnitude proportions; zero-sum polygon inequality x1≤sum others and monotonicity of (u²+A4)/(u+A2)² in u≥max xj² push to collinear boundary. At that boundary y_j≥0,sum y=1, maximize Q=(1+sum y^4)/(1+sum y²)². Independently differentiated pairwise smoothing in squared difference v: the sign is affine, increasing to an upper bound proportional to s²(1+A0)−1−B0≤0 using A0≤(1−s)², so averaging does not decrease Q. The uniform other coordinates y=1/(N−1) give NQ=N−2+1/(N−1). Equality in modulus and complex zero-sum forces the lone (N−1) value opposite N−1 copies of −1; inverse Fourier transform produces all c(N1_{x0}−1). N≥4 covers the strict classification; N=2,3 explicitly not claimed.
